P1.reason: A covers turn order, movement results, two-step restriction and setup; B leaves nineteen statements ungrouped, including all move effects, turn passing and initial state.

differences.reason: Board ordering with plus2 helps, but adding only the one-step effect (29) is arbitrary.
Corridor bounds as their own group helps; it is a recognisable edge-of-board rule.
Token position updates plus starting squares helps: clearly how tokens move and start.
Two-step permission with fresh tracking helps; captures the no-consecutive-double-step rule well.
Mixes hold/wait legality with stale tracking; partly coherent as pass moves but muddled.
Turn alternation and first player helps; a clean, nameable rule.
Roles alone is a weak group, but harmless as the player list.
Joins one-step legality and blocking with stale updates; the stale part hurts coherence.
Overlaps A4 and A8 with a mixed bag; redundant and hurts readability.
Step legality with bounds and blocking is a coherent movement rule, though merges several ideas.
Board ordering plus position effects of steps helps, but omits hold/wait effects.
